title: Refrigerator Sensor Failure
shortDescription: The refrigerator compartment thermistor is reading out of range or open circuit.
fullDescription: The Er code on Hisense French-door and side-by-side refrigerators indicates the main control board has lost communication with the fresh-food (refrigerator) compartment temperature sensor. The thermistor is either open, shorted, or producing values outside the expected resistance range. Cooling may continue at a default duty cycle but temperatures will not be regulated correctly.

causes.cause: Refrigerator compartment thermistor failed open
Loose or corroded sensor harness connector at the main board
Damaged wiring inside the liner or door hinge area
Defective main control board input channel

symptoms: Er flashing on the user interface display
Refrigerator section warming or freezing food
Compressor running continuously or short-cycling
Set-point adjustments have no effect on actual temperature

fixSteps.title: Power cycle the refrigerator
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the refrigerator from the wall outlet for 5 minutes, then plug it back in. A momentary controller glitch will clear with a hard reset.

fixSteps.title: Inspect the sensor harness
fixSteps.instruction: Locate the thermistor harness on the rear top of the fresh-food compartment. Reseat the connector and check for melted insulation or pinched wires.

fixSteps.title: Test the thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the sensor and measure resistance with a multimeter. At room temperature (25 C / 77 F) it should read approximately 5 kOhm. Out of range or open indicates a failed sensor.

fixSteps.title: Replace the sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Order the matching Hisense thermistor for your model and install in the same clip location, routing the harness back along the original path.

whenToCallPro: If the harness routes through a foamed-in cabinet liner that requires partial disassembly.

faq.q: Will my food spoil while Er is showing?
faq.a: Cooling usually continues but is not regulated. Move perishables to another fridge if temperatures rise above 40 F.

title: Evaporator Fan Motor Error
shortDescription: The evaporator fan in the freezer compartment has stopped or is not reporting RPM feedback.
fullDescription: EF indicates the freezer evaporator fan motor is not running at the expected speed. Hisense uses a 3-wire BLDC fan that reports tach pulses to the main board. If the board fails to detect rotation for several seconds the EF code is latched. Without the fan, cold air is not circulated and both compartments warm up.

causes.cause: Evaporator fan blade frozen against ice buildup
Failed BLDC evaporator fan motor
Defrost system failure causing ice to encase the fan
Broken fan harness wire

symptoms: Loud buzzing or chirping from the freezer that stops
Both compartments warm despite compressor running
Visible frost buildup on the rear freezer panel
EF appearing within minutes of opening and closing the freezer door

fixSteps.title: Manual defrost
fixSteps.instruction: Empty the freezer and unplug the unit for 24 hours with doors open and towels under the front. This melts any ice obstruction around the fan.

fixSteps.title: Access the fan
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the freezer rear panel screws to expose the evaporator and fan assembly. Inspect for ice or debris on the blade.

fixSteps.title: Test the fan motor
fixSteps.instruction: Apply 12 VDC briefly across the appropriate fan motor pins (per service sheet). If it does not spin smoothly, replace it.

fixSteps.title: Replace evaporator fan motor
fixSteps.instruction: Install the new BLDC fan motor and reconnect the harness. Reattach the rear panel before powering up.

whenToCallPro: If ice keeps reforming on the evaporator after replacement, the defrost heater or thermostat is the root cause.
videoSearchQuery: Hisense refrigerator EF evaporator fan replace

faq.q: Can I just chip the ice off the fan?
faq.a: No - using a tool risks puncturing the evaporator coil. Always melt the ice with time and warm air.

title: Defrost System Failure
shortDescription: The defrost cycle has not properly cleared frost from the evaporator within the expected time.
fullDescription: The dF code is logged when the bimetal defrost thermostat (or fuse) does not close within the defrost cycle timeout, or when the defrost heater draws no current. Hisense controllers run an adaptive defrost; persistent failure trips dF. Symptoms typically follow a slow buildup of frost over several days.

causes.cause: Open defrost heater element
Open bimetal defrost thermostat or thermal fuse
Failed defrost relay on the main control board
Sensor cluster unplugged after a previous repair

symptoms: Heavy frost on the back wall of the freezer
Refrigerator section warm because evaporator is iced over
Compressor runs continuously
dF on the display, possibly alternating with EF

fixSteps.title: Force a defrost
fixSteps.instruction: If the model supports a service mode, enter it and trigger a forced defrost. Otherwise unplug for 24 hours to fully melt the evaporator.

fixSteps.title: Test the heater
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, measure resistance across the defrost heater leads. A reading of OL means the element is open and must be replaced. Typical good reading is 20-50 Ohm.

fixSteps.title: Test the bimetal
fixSteps.instruction: Place the defrost bimetal in a freezer for 15 minutes and measure continuity. It should close cold and open at room temperature.

fixSteps.title: Replace failed component
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the open heater or bimetal with the correct Hisense service part. Verify the harness clip and routing match the original.

whenToCallPro: If both heater and bimetal test good but dF returns, the main board defrost relay is suspect and pro service is recommended.
videoSearchQuery: Hisense refrigerator dF defrost heater test

faq.q: How long should a defrost cycle last?
faq.a: Hisense adaptive defrost terminates when the bimetal opens, typically 15-25 minutes.

title: Ice Maker Sensor Error
shortDescription: The ice maker thermistor or optical sensor is out of range.
fullDescription: EE on Hisense models with built-in ice makers indicates the controller cannot read the ice maker thermistor or, on optical-bin models, the IR emitter/receiver pair has failed self-check. The ice maker is disabled until the fault is cleared.

causes.cause: Failed ice maker module thermistor
Frozen or wet harness connector at the ice maker
Ice or frost blocking the optical bin sensor
Failed ice maker module

symptoms: EE on the display
No new ice production
Bin reports full when empty or vice versa
Auger does not rotate when dispense is requested

fixSteps.title: Clean the optical sensors
fixSteps.instruction: On bin-mounted ice makers, wipe both small windows on the inside walls of the freezer compartment with a dry cloth. Frost and condensation cause false faults.

fixSteps.title: Reseat the ice maker harness
fixSteps.instruction: Lift out the ice maker and unplug the connector. Inspect for moisture or corrosion. Dry, reseat firmly, and reinstall.

fixSteps.title: Test thermistor resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance at the ice maker thermistor. Typical values are around 16 kOhm at -10 C. Replace if open or shorted.

fixSteps.title: Replace the ice maker module
fixSteps.instruction: If the thermistor is integrated in the module, replace the entire ice maker assembly with the model-specific Hisense part.

whenToCallPro: When the entire ice maker module needs replacement and water line work is required.
videoSearchQuery: Hisense refrigerator EE ice maker error

faq.q: Will the rest of the fridge keep working with EE?
faq.a: Yes. Cooling continues normally; only the ice maker is disabled.

title: Condenser Fan Motor Error
shortDescription: The condenser fan in the machine compartment is not turning at expected speed.
fullDescription: CF is reported when the condenser cooling fan does not return correct tach feedback to the main board. The condenser fan moves air across the hot condenser coil and across the compressor; without it, head pressures rise and cooling efficiency drops sharply.

causes.cause: Dust and lint blocking the fan blade
Failed condenser fan motor
Damaged fan harness from rodent activity
Main board fan driver fault

symptoms: Compressor running hot to the touch
Reduced cooling, especially in the freezer
CF code on display
Dust visible on the rear lower grille

fixSteps.title: Clean the condenser area
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the refrigerator, pull it from the wall, and remove the rear access panel. Vacuum dust from the condenser coil and the fan blade thoroughly.

fixSteps.title: Spin-test the fan blade
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, spin the fan blade by hand. It should rotate freely. Bearings that bind require motor replacement.

fixSteps.title: Test fan motor windings
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the fan and measure resistance across the windings. Typical values are 100-300 Ohm. Open or shorted readings indicate a bad motor.

fixSteps.title: Replace the condenser fan
fixSteps.instruction: Install the matching Hisense condenser fan motor, ensuring blade orientation and harness routing match the original.

whenToCallPro: If the compressor is hot and the system is short-cycling, the sealed system may also need pro evaluation.
videoSearchQuery: Hisense refrigerator CF condenser fan replace

faq.q: How often should I clean the condenser?
faq.a: Hisense recommends every 6-12 months, more often with pets in the home.

title: Freezer Sensor Failure
shortDescription: The freezer compartment thermistor is open, shorted, or out of range.
fullDescription: FZ identifies a failure of the freezer compartment temperature sensor. Without a valid freezer reading, the controller cannot regulate compressor run time and may default to a fixed duty cycle, leading to soft frozen foods or over-cooling.

causes.cause: Failed freezer thermistor
Loose connector at the main board
Wire break inside the freezer liner

symptoms: FZ shown on the display
Soft ice cream or partially thawed frozen goods
Heavy frost in some areas, none in others
Display freezer temperature stuck at default

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 5 minutes and reconnect to clear transient faults.

fixSteps.title: Test the freezer thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Locate the thermistor (typically clipped near the evaporator). Measure resistance: at -18 C it should be approximately 16 kOhm. Out of range = replace.

fixSteps.title: Replace the thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Install the replacement sensor in the same clip and route the wire along the original path. Reconnect at the main board.

whenToCallPro: If you are not comfortable removing the rear evaporator panel or working in the freezer cabinet.

faq.q: Is FZ the same as the Er code?
faq.a: Both indicate sensor failure, but Er typically means the fresh-food sensor and FZ specifically the freezer sensor.

title: Communication Error Between Boards
shortDescription: The user interface board and main control board are not communicating.
fullDescription: CO appears when the display PCB stops receiving valid serial messages from the main control board for several seconds. The fridge will typically continue cooling at the last commanded set points but the user interface becomes unresponsive.

causes.cause: Damaged or unseated ribbon cable between display and main board
Power surge damaged the UI MCU
Failed main control board

symptoms: CO on the display, all buttons unresponsive
Cooling appears to continue normally
Display flickers or turns off intermittently

fixSteps.title: Hard reset
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 5 minutes. Many CO faults result from a one-time communication glitch.

fixSteps.title: Reseat the ribbon cable
fixSteps.instruction: Open the top hinge cover or remove the upper rear panel to access the cable between the display and the main board. Unplug, inspect for bent pins, and firmly reconnect.

fixSteps.title: Replace the user interface board
fixSteps.instruction: If reseating does not clear CO and the main board outputs valid signals, replace the UI display assembly with the Hisense service part.

whenToCallPro: If the main board is suspected, professional diagnosis avoids unnecessary part swaps.

faq.q: Is my food at risk during a CO error?
faq.a: Usually not - the main board keeps running at the last set point. Verify temps with a thermometer.

title: Ambient Sensor Failure
shortDescription: The ambient (room) temperature sensor is out of range.
fullDescription: Hisense uses an ambient sensor to bias defrost and compressor run logic for hot or cold rooms. AD indicates the controller cannot read this sensor, falling back to a generic profile that may waste energy or cause inadequate cooling.

causes.cause: Failed ambient thermistor
Loose harness at the main board
Sensor location flooded with water from melted ice

symptoms: AD on display
Excessive run time during cool weather
Insufficient cooling on hot days
Incorrect ambient reading shown in service mode

fixSteps.title: Reseat the connector
fixSteps.instruction: Locate the ambient sensor (often near the bottom rear of the cabinet). Unplug and reconnect, ensuring the locking tab clicks.

fixSteps.title: Test resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Measure thermistor resistance at room temperature. Approximately 5 kOhm at 25 C is typical. Replace if shorted or open.

fixSteps.title: Replace the sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install the replacement ambient sensor and route the wire away from sharp edges and moving parts.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed; AD is one of the easier Hisense fault codes to fix at home.

faq.q: Will AD prevent the fridge from cooling?
faq.a: No, but cooling efficiency may suffer in extreme room temperatures.

title: Power Failure Notification
shortDescription: The refrigerator detected a recent power outage.
fullDescription: PF is an informational alert indicating a power loss occurred while the unit was running. Compartment temperatures may have risen during the outage. Press any button (typically Alarm or Power Freeze depending on model) to clear.

causes.cause: Utility power outage
Tripped GFCI or breaker
Loose plug or extension cord
Failed power supply on main board

symptoms: PF flashes on display after power restoration
Audible alert beeping
Possible thawed items in freezer

fixSteps.title: Acknowledge the alert
fixSteps.instruction: Press the Alarm/Mute or any front-panel key to dismiss PF. The fridge resumes normal operation.

fixSteps.title: Verify food safety
fixSteps.instruction: Check freezer items - if still rock-hard with ice crystals, they are safe. Discard refrigerator items that have been above 40 F for more than 4 hours.

fixSteps.title: Inspect outlet and breaker
fixSteps.instruction: If PF appears repeatedly without obvious outages, test the outlet with another appliance and check the breaker for loose connections.

whenToCallPro: If PF appears with no outage and the home electrical system has been verified.
videoSearchQuery: Hisense refrigerator PF power failure clear

faq.a: Most Hisense models do not allow disabling PF; it is intended to protect food safety.

title: Door Open Alarm
shortDescription: A refrigerator or freezer door has been left open beyond the alarm timeout.
fullDescription: dO is the door-ajar alarm. Hisense triggers it after approximately 2 minutes with any door switch reading open. The compartment lights flash and the unit beeps until the door is closed or the switch reports closed again.

causes.cause: Door left ajar by a user
Items on shelves preventing the door from sealing
Worn or warped door gasket
Stuck or failed reed/door switch

symptoms: Continuous beeping from the unit
dO on display
Interior lights stay on
Frost forming around the door opening

fixSteps.title: Close all doors firmly
fixSteps.instruction: Push each door closed and verify the gasket seals against the cabinet around the entire perimeter.

fixSteps.title: Check for obstructions
fixSteps.instruction: Make sure shelves, drawers, and items are not protruding past the door frame and preventing closure.

fixSteps.title: Inspect gasket
fixSteps.instruction: Look for tears, deformation, or food residue on the gasket. Clean with warm soapy water and replace if torn.

fixSteps.title: Test the door switch
fixSteps.instruction: Use a multimeter on the reed/door switch terminals. The switch should toggle between continuity and open as a magnet (or door) is moved away. Replace if stuck.

videoSearchQuery: Hisense refrigerator dO door open alarm

faq.q: Can I silence the alarm without closing the door?
faq.a: Pressing the Alarm/Mute button silences the audible beep but the dO code remains until the door is closed.
